name: Life insurance
intro: Term length and premium structure should match what the money is actually for — a mortgage isn't the same job as replacing income for a family.

glossary.def: Pays a fixed sum if you die within the term. Premiums usually stay flat for the whole term.
The payout shrinks over time, usually to track a repayment mortgage balance — cheaper than level term for the same starting cover.
Covers you for life rather than a fixed term, guaranteeing a payout eventually — priced much higher than term policies.
Premiums fixed at outset and won't rise; 'reviewable' premiums can increase at set points, often making a policy cheaper early and pricier later.

head: Best fits…
Level term
Decreasing term
Whole of life
rows: Lower premium for the same starting cover

checklist: Size the cover to the actual need — outstanding mortgage, or years of income multiplied by dependants.
Write the policy 'in trust' — it usually pays out faster and outside inheritance tax.
Check guaranteed vs reviewable premiums, and what triggers a review.
Decide whether a critical illness add-on is worth the extra premium for your situation.
Answer health questions accurately — non-disclosure is the most common reason claims are refused.
